metadata.title: Right inverses of Lévy processes: the excursion measure in the general case

nodes.name: Right inverse of a Lévy process
nodes.statement: A right inverse of a Lévy process $X = (X_t, t \ge 0)$ is any increasing process $K = (K_x, x \ge 0)$ such that $X_{K_x} = x$ for all $x \ge 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Increasing process whose composition with the Lévy process recovers the identity.

nodes.name: Partial right inverse
nodes.statement: A partial right inverse is any increasing process $K = (K_x, 0 \le x < \xi_K)$ such that $X_{K_x} = x$ for all $0 \le x < \xi_K$ for some random $\xi_K > 0$.

nodes.name: Lévy-Khintchine triplet
nodes.statement: Triplet $(a, \sigma^2, \Pi)$ with $a \in \mathbb{R}$, $\sigma^2 \ge 0$ and $\Pi$ measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with $\Pi(\{0\}) = 0$ and $\int_{\mathbb{R}} (1 \wedge y^2)\Pi(dy) < \infty$ characterizing the characteristic exponent $\psi(\lambda)$ of $X$.

nodes.name: Laplace exponent of the minimal partial right inverse
nodes.statement: $\rho(q) = -\ln E\left(e^{-qK_1}; \xi_K > 1\right) = \kappa_K + \eta_K q + \int_{(0,\infty)} (1 - e^{-qt}) \Lambda_K(dt)$.

nodes.name: Reflected process and local time
nodes.statement: The reflected process $Z = X - L$, where $L_t = \inf\{x \ge 0 : K_x > t\}$ for $0 \le t < K_{\xi_K}$ and $L_t = \xi_K$ for $t \ge K_{\xi_K}$; $L$ is a local time process of $Z$ at zero.

nodes.name: Excursion measure away from the right inverse
nodes.statement: $n^Z$ is the intensity measure on excursion space $(E, \mathcal{E})$ of the Poisson point process $(e^Z_x, 0 \le x < \xi)$ of excursions of $Z$ defined by $e^Z_x(r) = Z_{K_{x-} + r}$ for $0 \le r \le \Delta K_x$, and $0$ for $r \ge \Delta K_x$.

nodes.name: Excursion space $E$
nodes.statement: $E = \{\omega \in D : \omega(s) = 0 \text{ for all } s \ge \zeta(\omega) = \inf\{r > 0 : \omega(r) = 0\}\}$, equipped with the restriction $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{E}$ from the Borel $\sigma$-algebra on càdlàg paths.

nodes.name: Killed semi-group $P_t^\dagger$
nodes.statement: $P_t^\dagger(y, dz) = \mathbf{P}_y^\dagger(\{\omega : \omega(t) \in dz, \zeta(\omega) > t\})$ where $\mathbf{P}_y^\dagger$ is the law of $X$ started at $y$ frozen when hitting zero.

nodes.name: Ascending ladder time and height $(\tau, H)$
nodes.statement: Bivariate subordinator such that $H_x = X_{\tau_x} = \overline{X}_{\tau_x}$ visits all suprema $\overline{X}_t = \sup\{X_s, 0 \le s \le t\}$. Laplace exponent $k(\alpha,\beta) = \kappa + \eta\alpha + \delta\beta + \int_{[0,\infty)^2}(1 - e^{-\alpha s - \beta y})\Lambda(ds,dy)$.

nodes.name: Excursion measure away from the supremum
nodes.statement: $\widetilde{n}^R$ is the intensity measure of the Poisson point process $(e^R_x, x \ge 0)$ where $e^R_x(r) = R_{\tau_{x-} + r}$ for $0 \le r < \Delta\tau_x$ and $e^R_x(r) = \Delta H_x$ for $r \ge \Delta\tau_x$, with $R = X - \overline{X}$.

nodes.name: Concatenation of paths
nodes.statement: For $\omega_1$ with $\zeta^+(\omega_1) = \inf\{r > 0 : \omega_1(r) > 0\} < \infty$ and $\omega_2 \in D$: $\omega = \omega_1 \oplus \omega_2$ where $\omega(r) = \omega_1(r)$ for $0 \le r < \zeta^+(\omega_1)$ and $\omega(\zeta^+(\omega_1) + r) = \omega_2(r)$ for $r \ge 0$.

nodes.name: Hitting time and first passage time
nodes.statement: $T_{\{x\}} = \inf\{t \ge 0 : X_t = x\}$ is the hitting time of level $x$; $T_x^+ = \inf\{t \ge 0 : X_t \in (x, \infty)\}$ is the first passage time across level $x > 0$; $O_x = X_{T_x^+} - x$ is the overshoot.

nodes.name: Resolvent measure and density
nodes.statement: $U^q(dz) = \int_0^\infty e^{-qt} \mathbf{P}(X_t \in dz) dt$ is the $q$-resolvent measure; under the partial-right-inverse hypothesis it admits a bounded density $u^q(z)$ continuous except possibly at zero in the bounded variation case.

nodes.name: Lévy-Khintchine formula
nodes.statement: $E\left(e^{i\lambda X_t}\right) = e^{-t\psi(\lambda)}$, $\psi(\lambda) = -ia\lambda + \tfrac{1}{2}\sigma^2\lambda^2 + \int_{\mathbb{R}}(1 - e^{i\lambda y} + i\lambda y \mathbf{1}_{|y|\le 1}) \Pi(dy)$.

nodes.name: Fourier-Laplace transform of entrance laws (eq. 2)
nodes.statement: $\int_0^\infty e^{-qr} \int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{i\lambda y} n^Z_r(dy) dr = \dfrac{\rho(q) - i\lambda}{q + \psi(\lambda)} - \eta_K$.

nodes.name: Excursion measure $n^Z$ in the Gaussian case (eq. 3)
nodes.statement: $n^Z(d\omega) = \dfrac{2}{\sigma^2} n^X(d\omega; \omega(s) < 0 \text{ for all } 0 < s < \varepsilon)$ when $\sigma^2 > 0$.

nodes.name: Excursion measure $n^Z$ in the bounded variation case (eq. 4)
nodes.statement: $n^Z(d\omega) = \dfrac{1}{b}\int_{\mathbb{R}} \mathbf{P}_y^\dagger(d\omega) \Pi(dy)$, where $b = a - \int_{\mathbb{R}} y \mathbf{1}_{|y|\le 1}\Pi(dy) > 0$.

nodes.name: Quintuple law (eq. 12)
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{P}(T_x^+ - G_{T_x^+ -} \in dt, G_{T_x^+ -} \in ds, O_x \in dw, x - \overline{X}_{T_x^+ -} \in dy; T_x^+ < \infty) = \Lambda(dt, du + y) U(x - dy, ds)$.

nodes.name: Hitting time decomposition (eq. 13)
nodes.statement: $T_{\{x\}} = T_x^+ + \widetilde{T}_{\{-O_x\}}$ a.s. on $\{T_x^+ < \infty\}$, where $\widetilde{T}_{\{-O_x\}} = \inf\{t \ge 0 : \widetilde{X}_t = -O_x\}$ for $\widetilde{X}$ independent of $(T_x^+, O_x)$.

nodes.name: Discretization of $\rho(q)$ (eq. 14)
nodes.statement: $\rho(q) = -\ln \lim_{n\to\infty} E(e^{-qK_1^{(n)}}) = -\ln \lim_{n\to\infty}(1 - z_n/2^n)^{2^n} = \lim_{n\to\infty} z_n$, where $z_n = 2^n E(1 - e^{-qT_{\{2^{-n}\}}})$.

nodes.name: Evans' construction of right inverses
nodes.statement: Recursively define dyadic hitting times of levels $k/2^n$ and pass to a pathwise limit to obtain the minimal right-continuous partial right inverse $K_x$.
input: Lévy process $X = (X_t, t \ge 0)$ admitting partial right inverses
output: Minimal partial right inverse $K_x = \inf_{y > x} \sup_{n \ge 0} K^{(n)}_y$, finite for $0 \le x < \xi_K$

nodes.name: Alternative ladder-based construction $\widetilde{K}(n)$
nodes.statement: Approximate $K$ by the ascending ladder time process $\tau$, jumping over excursions of height $> 2^{-n}$ by adding the excursion length plus the return time to the starting height; iterate.
output: Process $\widetilde{K}_x(n)$ approximating $K_x$ such that $X_{\widetilde{K}_x(n)}$ has no jumps of size $> 2^{-n}$

nodes.name: Theorem 1 — Excursion measure away from the right inverse
nodes.statement: $n^Z(d\omega) = (\widetilde{n}^R \oplus K)(d\omega)$, where the kernel $K(\omega_1, d\omega_2) = \mathbf{P}_{\omega_1(\zeta^+(\omega_1))}^\dagger(d\omega_2)$ if $\zeta^+(\omega_1) < \infty$ and $\delta_0$ otherwise.
assumptions: $X$ is a Lévy process possessing a partial right inverse
conclusions: The excursion measure $n^Z$ away from the right inverse equals the image under concatenation of $K(\omega_1, d\omega_2)\widetilde{n}^R(d\omega_1)$

nodes.name: Corollary 2 — Entrance laws of $n^Z$
nodes.statement: $n^Z_t(dz) = \widetilde{n}^R_t(dz) + \int_{[0,t]\times(0,\infty)} P^\dagger_{t-s}(y, dz) \Lambda(ds, dy)$, and the semi-group of $n^Z$ is $(P^\dagger_t(y,dz), t\ge 0)$.
assumptions: $X$ is a Lévy process possessing a partial right inverse
conclusions: Explicit formula for entrance laws of $n^Z$
Semi-group of $n^Z$ is the killed semi-group $P^\dagger_t$

nodes.name: Proposition 3 — Laplace exponent of $K$
nodes.statement: $\rho(q) = \kappa + \eta q + \int_{[0,\infty)\times[0,\infty)} \left(1 - e^{-qs}\dfrac{u^q(-y)}{u^q(0)}\right) \Lambda(ds, dy)$, with $u^q(0) = u^q(0+)$. The characteristics $(\kappa_K, \eta_K, \Lambda_K)$ are given by $\kappa_K = \kappa + \int \mathbf{P}(T_{\{-y\}}=\infty)\Lambda(ds,dy)$, $\eta_K = \eta$, $\Lambda_K(dt) = \int \mathbf{P}(s + T_{\{-y\}} \in dt; T_{\{-y\}} < \infty)\Lambda(ds, dy)$.
assumptions: $X$ is a Lévy process possessing a partial right inverse
conclusions: Closed-form expression (8) for the Laplace exponent $\rho(q)$

nodes.name: Corollary 4 — Recurrent case equivalence
nodes.statement: A recurrent Lévy process has a partial right inverse iff it has a full right inverse.
conclusions: Existence of a partial right inverse is equivalent to existence of a full right inverse

nodes.name: Lemma 5 — Limit of $\hat{z}_n$
nodes.statement: $\lim_{n\to\infty} \hat{z}_n = \int_{(0,\infty)^2} \left(1 - e^{-qt}\dfrac{u^q(-h)}{u^q(0)}\right) \Lambda(dt, dh)$.
conclusions: The auxiliary sequence $\hat{z}_n$ converges to the displayed integral expression

nodes.name: Lemma 6 — Limit of $\widetilde{z}_n$
nodes.statement: $\lim_{n\to\infty} \widetilde{z}_n = \kappa + \int_{(0,\infty)} (1 - e^{-qu}) \Lambda(dt, \{0\})$.
conclusions: The complementary sequence $\widetilde{z}_n$ converges to the displayed expression

nodes.name: Lemma 7 — $\widetilde{K}(n)$ is a bivariate subordinator
nodes.statement: $((\widetilde{K}_x(n), X_{\widetilde{K}_x(n)}), x \ge 0)$ is a bivariate subordinator with drift $(\eta, 1)$ and Lévy measure $\widetilde{\Lambda}_n(dt, dz) = \Lambda(dt, dz \cap [0, 2^{-n}]) + \int_{[0,\infty)\times(2^{-n},\infty)} \mathbf{P}(s + T_{\{-y\}} \in dt, 0 \in dz)\Lambda(ds, dy)$.
assumptions: $\widetilde{K}_x(n)$ is the alternative ladder-based approximation of Section 2
conclusions: $(\widetilde{K}(n), X \circ \widetilde{K}(n))$ is a bivariate subordinator with explicit drift and Lévy measure

nodes.name: Lemma 8 — Identification of $K$ as inf-sup of $\widetilde{K}(n)$
nodes.statement: $K_x = \inf_{y > x} \sup_{n \ge 0} \widetilde{K}_{L_n(y)}(n)$, where $L_n(y) = \inf\{x \ge 0 : X_{\widetilde{K}_x(n)} \ge y - 2^{-n}\}$.
conclusions: Minimal right inverse $K$ admits inf-sup representation through $\widetilde{K}(n)$

nodes.name: Lemma 9 — Subsequential convergence $\widetilde{K}_x(n_k) \to K_x$
nodes.statement: There is a subsequence $(n_k)_{k\ge 0}$ such that $\lim_{k\to\infty} \widetilde{K}_x(n_k) = K_x$ a.s. for all $x \ge 0$.
conclusions: Almost-sure convergence along a subsequence to the minimal right inverse $K_x$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5
nodes.statement: Use the resolvent identity $E(e^{-qT_{\{x\}}}) = u^q(x)/u^q(0)$ together with (12) to expand $\hat{z}_n$ as a double integral; then apply weak convergence of $\vartheta_{n,h}$ to $\delta_{(0,0)}$ via unit drift of $H$, plus Dominated Convergence with explicit $\Lambda$-integrable bound.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6
nodes.statement: Apply [1, Theorem VI.18] giving $E(1 - e^{-qT_x^+}) = k(q,0) V^q(x)$ with $V^q(x) \sim x$, then split $\widetilde{z}_n$ on $\{O_{2^{-n}} = 0\} \cup \{T_{2^{-n}}^+ = \infty\}$ and pass to the limit using $\eta = 0$ in unbounded variation.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3
nodes.statement: In the unbounded variation case, $\rho(q) = \lim z_n = \lim(\hat{z}_n + \widetilde{z}_n)$ via (14)-(15) combined with Lemmas 5 and 6; in the bounded variation case appeal to [8, Section 5.3]. Invert the Laplace transform $u^q(-y)/u^q(0) = E(e^{-qT_{\{-y\}}}; T_{\{-y\}} < \infty)$ to read off the characteristics.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 4
nodes.statement: If $X$ is recurrent then $\kappa = 0$ and $\mathbf{P}(T_{\{-y\}} = \infty) = 0$ for all $y$; substituting into the formula for $\kappa_K$ in (9) gives $\kappa_K = 0$, so the partial right inverse is in fact a full right inverse.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 and Corollary 2
nodes.statement: By [8, Theorem 2], $n^Z$ is uniquely determined by its entrance laws. Verify (7) satisfies (2) using a Wiener-Hopf computation and the joint transform of the convolution term, then check that the RHS of (6) is Markovian with semi-group $P_t^\dagger$ and has the entrance laws of (7).

nodes.name: Alternative proof of Proposition 3 (Appendix A)
nodes.statement: Approximate $K_x = \lim_k \widetilde{K}_x(n_k)$ by Lemma 9; the Laplace exponent of $\widetilde{K}_x(n_k)$ from Lemma 7 yields, in the limit, the formula (8) for $\rho(q)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7
nodes.statement: By standard thinning of Poisson point processes, $((\Delta\widetilde{K}_x(n), \Delta\widetilde{H}_x(n)), 0 \le x < S_1(n))$ has intensity $\Lambda(dt, dz \cap [0, 2^{-n}])$ run up to an exponential time; apply strong Markov at $T_m(n)$ and superposition of independent PPPs.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8
nodes.statement: Since $X_{\widetilde{K}_x(n)}$ has no jumps of size exceeding $2^{-n}$, $x - 2^{-n} \le X_{\widetilde{K}_x(n)} \le x$. Define $\widetilde{K}_x = \liminf_n \widetilde{K}_{L_n(x)}(n)$; quasi-left continuity of $X$ gives $X_{\widetilde{K}_x} = x$; minimality of $K$ then forces $\inf_{y>x} \widetilde{K}_y = K_x$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9
nodes.statement: Lemma 7 shows $\widetilde{H}(n)$ has drift 1, so $\widetilde{H}_x(n) \to x$ in probability and a.s. along a subsequence; combined with Lemma 8 this forces $\widetilde{K}_x(n_k) \to K_x$ a.s.

nodes.name: Apply quintuple law to expand $\hat{z}_n$
nodes.statement: Use $E(e^{-qT_{\{x\}}}) = u^q(x)/u^q(0)$ and (12) to write $E(1 - e^{-q(T_x^+ + \widetilde{T}_{\{-O_x\}})} \mathbf{1}_{O_x > 0})$ as a triple integral over $\Lambda(dt,dh)$ and $U(ds, x - dy)$.

nodes.name: Define measure $\vartheta_{n,h}$ and target weak limit
nodes.statement: Set $\vartheta_{n,h}(ds,dy) = \mathbf{1}_{[0, 2^{-n}\wedge h]}(y) 2^n U(ds, 2^{-n} - dy)$ on $[0,\infty)^2$; show $\vartheta_{n,h} \to \delta_{(0,0)}$ weakly using unit drift of $H$.

nodes.name: Pointwise weak convergence of $\int f \, d\vartheta_{n,h}$
nodes.statement: For bounded continuous $f(s,y) = (1 - e^{-q(t+s)}) u^q(-h+y)/u^q(0)$, conclude $\int f \, d\vartheta_{n,h} \to f(0,0)$.

nodes.name: Establish $\Lambda$-integrable upper bound (21)
nodes.statement: Decompose the integrand into three terms and bound by $(1-e^{-qt}) + [\tfrac{1}{2}k(q,0) + k(0,\rho(q))](1\wedge h) + (1 - u^q(-h)/u^q(0))$ using $\vartheta_{n,h}([0,\infty)^2) \le 1$ and the decreasing property of $x \mapsto e^{-\rho(q)x} u^q(-x)$.

nodes.name: Apply Dominated Convergence and Fatou
nodes.statement: Use Fatou to show $\liminf \hat{z}_n \ge \int (1 - u^q(-h)/u^q(0)) \Lambda(dt, dh)$; since $z_n \to \rho(q) < \infty$ and $\hat{z}_n \le z_n$, the integrand is $\Lambda$-integrable; DCT then yields (16).

nodes.name: Apply [1, Theorem VI.18] for first passage Laplace transform
nodes.statement: Use $E(1 - e^{-qT_x^+}) = k(q,0) V^q(x)$ with $V^q(x) = \int_0^\infty E(e^{-q\tau_s}; H_s \le x) ds$; note $V^q(x) \sim x$ as $x \downarrow 0$ since $v^q(0+) = 1$ from unit drift of $H$.

nodes.name: Express $\widetilde{z}_n$ via first passage transform
nodes.statement: Rewrite $\widetilde{z}_n = 2^n E(1 - e^{-qT_{2^{-n}}^+} \mathbf{1}_{O_{2^{-n}} = 0 \text{ or } T_{2^{-n}}^+ = \infty})$ using $\eta = 0$ in the unbounded variation case.

nodes.name: Pass to the limit in $n$ to obtain (16)-style identity
nodes.statement: Combine the two preceding steps and (5) to obtain $\lim \widetilde{z}_n = \kappa + \int_{(0,\infty)} (1 - e^{-qu})\Lambda(dt, \{0\})$.

nodes.name: Combine $\hat{z}_n$ and $\widetilde{z}_n$ via decomposition (15)
nodes.statement: Unbounded variation case: by (14) $\rho(q) = \lim z_n$, and (15) writes $z_n = \hat{z}_n + \widetilde{z}_n$; Lemmas 5 and 6 give the two limits whose sum equals (8).

nodes.name: Bounded variation case via prior reference
nodes.statement: When $X$ is of bounded variation appeal to [8, Section 5.3], where $\rho(q)$ and the relation of $K$ to ladder processes are computed.

nodes.name: Read off characteristics by inverting $u^q(-y)/u^q(0)$
nodes.statement: Invert the Laplace transform $u^q(-y)/u^q(0) = E(e^{-qT_{\{-y\}}}; T_{\{-y\}} < \infty)$; using $u^q(0) = u^q(0+)$ this entails $\mathbf{P}(T_{\{0\}} = 0) = 1$ and yields $(\kappa_K, \eta_K, \Lambda_K)$ as in (9).

nodes.name: Recurrence implies $\kappa = 0$ and $\mathbf{P}(T_{\{-y\}}=\infty) = 0$
nodes.statement: Since $X$ recurrent does not drift to $-\infty$, $\kappa = 0$; recurrence forces $\mathbf{P}(T_{\{-y\}} = \infty) = 0$ for all $y \in \mathbb{R}$.

nodes.name: Substitute into formula (9) for $\kappa_K$
nodes.statement: Plug the two vanishing quantities into $\kappa_K = \kappa + \int \mathbf{P}(T_{\{-y\}}=\infty)\Lambda(ds, dy) = 0$, so $K$ is a full right inverse.

nodes.name: Reduce to checking entrance laws
nodes.statement: By [8, Theorem 2], the excursion measure $n^Z$ is uniquely determined by its entrance laws; therefore it suffices to verify (7) satisfies (2).

nodes.name: Wiener-Hopf transform of $\widetilde{n}^R_t$ term
nodes.statement: Compute $\int_0^\infty e^{-qt}\int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{i\lambda y}\widetilde{n}^R_t(dy)dt = k(q, -i\lambda)/(q+\psi(\lambda)) - \eta$ via the Wiener-Hopf factorization $k(q,0)\hat{k}(q,0)/(k(q,-i\lambda)\hat{k}(q,i\lambda)) = q/(q+\psi(\lambda))$.

nodes.name: Joint transform of $\Lambda$-convolution term
nodes.statement: Integrate the second term of (7) using the identity $E_y(e^{i\lambda X_{\gamma(q)}}; T_{\{0\}} > \gamma(q)) = qe^{i\lambda y}/(q+\psi(\lambda)) - (u^q(-y)/u^q(0))(q/(q+\psi(\lambda)))$.

nodes.name: Sum equals $\rho(q) - i\lambda$
nodes.statement: Adding the two transforms and using (5) yields $k(q,-i\lambda) + \int e^{-qs}(e^{i\lambda y} - q u^q(-y)/u^q(0))\Lambda(ds,dy) = \rho(q) - i\lambda$, which proves (7) implies (2).

nodes.name: Verify Markov structure of $(\widetilde{n}^R \oplus K)$
nodes.statement: Check the RHS of (6) is Markovian with semi-group $P_t^\dagger$ and confirm its entrance laws coincide with the RHS of (7), using $\widetilde{n}^R(\{\zeta^+(\omega_1)\in ds, \omega_1(\zeta^+(\omega_1))\in dy\}) = \Lambda(ds, dy)$.

nodes.name: Approximate $K_x$ by subsequence (Lemma 9)
nodes.statement: Use Lemma 9 to write $K_x = \lim_{k\to\infty} \widetilde{K}_x(n_k)$ a.s., reducing computation of the Laplace exponent to that of the approximations.

nodes.name: Limit of Laplace exponents from Lemma 7
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 7 to identify the Laplace exponent of $\widetilde{K}_1(n_k)$ and pass to the limit, recovering $\rho(q) = \eta q + \int_{[0,\infty)\times\{0\}} (1 - e^{-qs})\Lambda(ds,dy) + \int_{[0,\infty)\times(0,\infty)} (1 - e^{-qs} E(e^{-qT_{\{-y\}}}))\Lambda(ds,dy)$.

nodes.name: Thinning gives intensity $\Lambda(dt, dz\cap[0,2^{-n}])$
nodes.statement: By standard thinning of $((\Delta\tau_x, \Delta H_x), x \ge 0)$, the kept points $((\Delta\widetilde{K}_x(n), \Delta\widetilde{H}_x(n)), 0 \le x < S_1(n))$ form a PPP with intensity $\Lambda(dt, dz\cap [0,2^{-n}])$ run to independent exponential time $S_1(n)$.

nodes.name: Mark removed points by $T_{\{-\Delta H_x\}}$
nodes.statement: For removed points (excursion height $> 2^{-n}$) attach independent return times to compute $\mathbf{P}(\Delta\widetilde{K}_{S_1(n)} \in dt, \Delta\widetilde{H}_{S_1(n)} \in dz)$ as the displayed integral.

nodes.name: Iterate via strong Markov and PPP superposition
nodes.statement: By the strong Markov property at $T_m(n)$, removed-point vectors are i.i.d.; standard superposition of PPPs yields the bivariate subordinator with drift $(\eta, 1)$ and Lévy measure $\widetilde{\Lambda}_n$.

nodes.name: Pinch $X_{\widetilde{K}_x(n)}$ by $2^{-n}$
nodes.statement: Construction of $\widetilde{K}(n)$ ensures $X_{\widetilde{K}_x(n)}$ has no jumps exceeding $2^{-n}$; hence $x - 2^{-n} \le X_{\widetilde{K}_x(n)} \le x$.

nodes.name: Define $\widetilde{K}_x = \liminf$ and show $X_{\widetilde{K}_x} = x$
nodes.statement: Define $\widetilde{K}_x = \liminf_n \widetilde{K}_{L_n(x)}(n)$; right- and quasi-left-continuity of $X$ [1, Prop. I.7] yield $X_{\widetilde{K}_x} = x$ a.s.

nodes.name: Conclude $\inf_{y>x} \widetilde{K}_y = K_x$ by minimality
nodes.statement: $\widetilde{K}_x$ extended to $\mathbb{Q}_+$ is a right-continuous right inverse; minimality of $K$ forces $\inf_{y>x}\widetilde{K}_y = K_x$.

nodes.name: Drift 1 of $\widetilde{H}(n)$ via Lemma 7
nodes.statement: Lemma 7 gives drift 1 for $\widetilde{H}(n)$, so $\widetilde{H}_x(n) \ge x$ and $\widetilde{H}_x(n) \to x$ in probability as $n \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Subsequence with a.s. convergence
nodes.statement: Extract subsequence $(n_k)$ along which $\widetilde{H}_x(n_k) \to x$ a.s.; combined with Lemma 8 obtain $\widetilde{K}_x(n_k) \to K_x$ a.s.

nodes.name: Initialize dyadic stopping times
nodes.statement: Set $T_0^{(n)} = 0$ and recursively $T_{k+1}^{(n)} = \inf\{t \ge T_k^{(n)} : X_t = (k+1)/2^n\}$ for $k \ge 1$.

nodes.name: Build piecewise-constant approximation $K^{(n)}_x$
nodes.statement: Define $K^{(n)}_x = T_k^{(n)}$ for $k/2^n \le x < (k+1)/2^n$, $k \ge 0$.

nodes.name: Pass to the inf-sup limit
nodes.statement: Set $K_x = \inf_{y > x} \sup_{n \ge 0} K^{(n)}_y$; if finite for $0 \le x < \xi_K$ this is the minimal partial right inverse.

nodes.name: Initialize via ladder time $\tau$ until first large excursion
nodes.statement: Fix $n \ge 0$. Let $S_1(n) = \inf\{x \ge 0 : \Delta H_x > 2^{-n}\}$; set $\widetilde{K}_x(n) = \tau_x$ for $0 \le x < S_1(n)$.

nodes.name: Jump over excursions of height $> 2^{-n}$
nodes.statement: At $S_1(n)$ set $\widetilde{K}_{S_1(n)}(n) = \inf\{t \ge \tau_{S_1(n)} : X_t = X_{\tau_{S_1(n)-}}\}$, adding excursion length plus return time to the starting height.

nodes.name: Iterate using strong Markov property
nodes.statement: Restart from $X^{(m)}(n)_t = X_{T_m(n) + t} - X_{T_m(n)}$ and define $S_{m+1}(n)$ analogously; recursively extend $\widetilde{K}(n)$ to all $x \ge 0$.

nodes.name: Singularity of $n^Z$ and $n^X$ in unbounded variation case
nodes.statement: When $\sigma^2 = 0$ and $X$ is of unbounded variation, a.e. excursion under $n^X$ starts positive and ends negative while a.e. excursion under $\widetilde{n}^R$ starts negative; hence by Theorem 1, $n^Z$ and $n^X$ are mutually singular, in contrast to (3) for $\sigma^2 > 0$.

nodes.name: When $\Lambda(\{0\}, dy)$ is non-zero
nodes.statement: $\Lambda(\{0\}, dy)$ is the zero measure unless $X$ can jump into its new supremum from its current supremum; this requires positive ladder-time drift $\eta > 0$, which only happens when $X$ is of bounded variation.

nodes.name: Identity complementing the quintuple law
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{P}(T_x^+ \in dt, O_x = 0) dx = \mathbf{P}(T_x^+ = G_{T_x^+ -} \in dt, O_x = 0, x - \overline{X}_{T_x^+ -} = 0; T_x^+ < \infty) dx = U(dt, dx)$. Pointed out by Andreas Kyprianou; complements (12).
